title: Batched Latency Mitigation — Standup Cheat Sheet
content:
Standup snapshot — purpose: compact reference for engineers on shift and a quick checklist for experiments and mitigations. Informal notes; keep it short and actionable.

Date: 2026-03-10 — evening sync (covering last 72h)
Attendees: Asha, Evan, Priya, Jonah, Marta

Quick summary:
- Spike this sprint focused on reducing 95th/99th token latency regressions seen during mixed-workload bursts.
- Approaches under test: adaptive queuing window, jitter-smoothed batching, kernel-level spin/yield tune, and cache primer on cold-starts.
- Running two live experiments behind feature flags (exp-a: adaptive-window-v1, exp-b: jitter-smoothing-v2).

Observations / findings (short):
- Adaptive-window-v1 (exp-a): 7% end-to-end median latency decrease on small requests, but tail (p99) improved only when combined with kernel-spin=soft. Alone, it increased small-batch CPU churn. (Metric: median 78ms -> 72ms; p99 420ms -> 395ms when spin=soft; without spin change p99 bumped to 435ms)
- Jitter-smoothing-v2 (exp-b): reduced straggler batch formation by smoothing arrival bucketing; best for bursty client patterns. Observed fewer long-wait batches but slightly higher token coalescing variance. Useful for interactive traffic.
- Kernel spin/yield change: switching to low-spin for idle detections reduced GPU context-switch overhead in high-concurrency tests. Need to measure power/thermal impact (lab test scheduled).
- Cache primer (short prewarm RPC to fill route-level prefix cache): improved first-request latency for long sequences — but increases overall request count and needs quota consideration. Good candidate for Dedicated customers where warmup cost is amortized.

Playbook snippets (for oncall and engineers):
- If high tail latency after deploy: flip exp-a off, revert kernel-spin to previous, and ramp jitter-smoothing-bias to 0.8.
- If bursty p95 spikes persist: enable jitter-smoothing-v2 and temporarily raise max-batch-wait-ms by +5ms while monitoring token cost.
- Cold-start hits for model X: enable cache-primer for route X (flag: primer/route-x=true) and run warmup script with sample prompts for 2 minutes.

Action items (owners + ETA):
- Evan: finish smoke tests for kernel-spin low-spin profile on pcluster-7; target 2026-03-12 EOD. (JIRA:INF-1334)
- Priya: add cost-telemetry to cache-primer flow (incremental tokens and estimated $ per 1k warmups). Target 2026-03-15.
- Jonah: validate thermal/power effect from spin workaround in lab; log CPU/GPU power deltas. Target 2026-03-14.
- Marta: create A/B dashboard for exp-a vs exp-b with 1h, 6h, 24h slices and p50/p95/p99. Target 2026-03-13 morning.
- Asha: draft customer-facing note for Dedicated customers describing primer tradeoffs. Target 2026-03-17.

Experiment details (for reproducibility):
- exp-a: adaptive-window-v1
  - config: base-window-ms=4, max-window-ms=30, decay-factor=0.85, sampling-rate=20% of traffic
  - kernel flag: spin=soft (optional in combo)
  - traffic: sampled production traffic (tier=dev and staging sim)
  - metrics captured: request-latency-per-token, batch-size-distribution, batch-wait-ms, cpu-thread-blocks

- exp-b: jitter-smoothing-v2
  - config: jitter-bin-ms=2, smoothing-alpha=0.6, coalesce-threshold=8 tokens
  - traffic: interactive client subset (chat routes)
  - metrics: orphan-batch-count, inter-arrival-variance, p95/p99 tail behavior

Notes to self / loose thoughts (brainstorm fragments):
- Could route small-chat to an aggressive micro-batcher with preemption if we detect long sequence backfill. Need simulation.
- Consider a lightweight admission token for primer calls so we can charge/attribute warmups to route owners.
- Kernel-level hack: try a quick-return path for empty-KV hits to avoid full context enqueue; might shave 20-30µs. Risk: code complexity.
- Thought: integrate primer decisions into rollout rules in Console (so customers can opt-in per model/route).

Incidents / anomalies this week:
- Mar 9 03:12 UTC: transient p99 spike on route /chat-stream-512 correlating with gc sweep in auxiliary process. Root cause: helper process memory compaction paused the network thread for ~150ms. Mitigation: move compaction to staggered windows and add backoff. (Assigned: infra; ticket INF-1287)
- Mar 10 01:48 UTC: small regression after deploying kernel micro-optimizations to staging — observed increased batch fragmentation when client-RTT was >120ms. Rollback performed. Roll-forward will include jitter-smoothing.

Open questions (prioritized):
- What is the long-term cost model for primer at scale for Hosted customers? (Priya to model)
- Should we make kernel-spin=soft default for high-concurrency clusters? Tradeoffs unknown for thermal costs. (Jonah lab tests)
- How to expose batch/coalesce diagnostics in Console without leaking internal scheduling heuristics? (Product + DevExp conversation needed)

Short checklist for next handoff (night team):
- Confirm exp-a flag states and revert plan in mob-runbook.
- Verify A/B dashboard ingest for last 24h.
- Keep primer off for Hosted default; Dedicated only behind opt-in.
- Watch infra gc compaction schedule and confirm stagger rollout.

Misc notes (looser, copyable):
- Useful queries:
  - sum by(route) (count_over_time(requests[1h])) to find bursty routes
  - hist(mean_over_time(batch_wait_ms[5m])) to detect slow coalescing

- Quick command to toggle feature flags (dev cluster):
  - ./tools/flags set serving.runtime.exp-a false --env=dev --reason=\"rollback-night\"

Ending thought: we have several complementary knobs; aim for small, reversible changes per deploy. Avoid entangling primer and queue-window in same rollouts unless we've got tight dashboards.

-- end of cheat sheet (feel free to chop or redistribute sections into runbooks).
